title: Subclinical Gastrointestinal Involvement in Juvenile Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
off: Evaluation of Subclinical Gastrointestinal Involvement in Juvenile Systemic Lupus Erythematosus at Assiut University Children Hospital
summary: This cross-sectional case-control study aims to evaluate fecal calprotectin levels and intestinal ultrasound findings for the detection of subclinical gastrointestinal involvement in children with juvenile systemic lupus erythematosus compared with healthy controls.
desc:
Juvenile systemic lupus erythematosus is a chronic multisystem autoimmune disease. Gastrointestinal involvement may be under-recognized and can be subclinical.

This observational study will measure fecal calprotectin and perform intestinal ultrasound in children with JSLE and age- and sex-matched healthy controls to assess subclinical gastrointestinal involvement.
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Children less than 18 years of age
* Diagnosis of juvenile systemic lupus erythematosus according to SLICC criteria
* Disease duration of at least 3 months
* Age- and sex-matched healthy controls
* Written informed consent from parents or legal guardians

Exclusion Criteria:

* \- Established diagnosis of inflammatory bowel disease or other primary gastrointestinal disorder
* Significant gastrointestinal manifestations (persistent abdominal pain, diarrhea, vomiting, GI bleeding, significant unexplained weight loss)
* Active gastrointestinal infection within the preceding 4 weeks
* Antibiotics, probiotics, or NSAIDs within the 2 weeks preceding stool sample collection
* Other autoinflammatory or overlapping autoimmune diseases
* Chronic liver or renal disease unrelated to JSLE

arms.d: Children with JSLE according to SLICC criteria with disease duration of at least 3 months.
